groups.trust_reason: Logic that decides what may leave, what is trusted or how evidence is produced belongs in the kernel so every surface gets the same answer and none can weaken it; surfaces only display and relay user decisions.

Interactive review screens over private files: the browser is only the screen for the local kernel (companion), the page is untrusted for approvals, and the same views are loaded inside the desktop shell.
Needs microphone, snapshots of the real filesystem or running agent-written code under native isolation, which a browser tab cannot grant or enforce.
Agent and terminal entry points to the same kernel; they cannot approve interactively and an MCP client is a separate principal whose results are public-labelled unless released.

Public, no-install material for recipients and reviewers (verifier page, sample capsules, guides, demo kit); contains no private data and trusts nothing the sender hosts because verification runs in the reader's browser.
Needs a shared service (escrow, organisation tenancy); only claimable after hosted-mode isolation, key management and honest wording are validated.
Chat services and phones are untrusted transports; consequential approvals need a passkey with an exact-bytes summary on the device, and the kernel stays on the user's machine.
No kernel in the extension; it talks to the local companion, every web page is untrusted, and it needs the narrowest permissions and an origin allowlist.
